summary.text: Basalt is a fine-grained volcanic rock formed when runny lava rich in magnesium and iron cools quickly at or near the surface of a rocky planet or moon.
More than 90% of all volcanic rock on Earth is basalt, and its low silica content keeps its lava runny enough to spread over great areas before it hardens.
Most basalt on Earth forms when hot mantle rock creeps upward, the pressure on it drops, and it partly melts.

facts.label: Elsewhere in space
facts.value: The lunar maria are flood-basalt plains

items.prompt: Magma with exactly the chemistry of basalt stays deep underground and cools very slowly. Which rock does it become?
items.explain: Slow-cooling, coarse-grained gabbro has the same chemical makeup and minerals as fast-cooling, fine-grained basalt.

items.prompt: Basalt lava can race across the land and spread over huge areas before it sets. What makes it so runny?
items.explain: Basalt lava has low viscosity because of its relatively low silica content, so it flows quickly and spreads far.

items.prompt: A chunk of basalt is full of small round holes. How did they get there?

options.label: Gas bubbles were trapped as the lava hardened
Rainwater dissolved soft minerals over time
Burrowing sea creatures tunnelled into it
Crystals fell out as the rock weathered

items.explain: Dissolved gases bubble out of the magma as it nears the surface, and the lava solidifies before the gas can escape, leaving holes called vesicles.

items.prompt: Hot mantle rock slowly creeps upward without being heated any further, yet it starts to melt. Why?

options.label: Friction as it moves adds a lot of heat
Seawater seeps down and boils it
Contact with the cold crust melts it
Less pressure lowers its melting point

items.explain: As the rising rock is under less pressure, its melting point drops enough for it to partly melt and make basaltic magma.

items.prompt: Roughly what share of all the volcanic rock on Earth is basalt?
items.explain: More than 90% of all volcanic rock on Earth is basalt.

items.prompt: Geologists study the chemistry of basalt to learn about places no one can visit. Which place does it tell them about?

options.label: The bottom of the oceans' water
The far side of the Sun

items.explain: Basaltic magmas are thought to come from the upper mantle, so their chemistry gives clues to processes deep inside the Earth.
